# Cart bundle (SFCC-11) — executable build plan

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Zimmermann cart drawer and its line-item system — SFCC-315, 270, 795, 271, 272, 250, 275 — as prescribed by those seven Sprint 5 cards, as designed in Figma file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` nodes `9323-65888/65895/65983/66104` (DEFAULT PAGE TEMPLATE) plus the CART MERGE, WISHLIST, INTERNATIONAL, EMPTY BAG and OOS state groups across all four breakpoints, as approached by the FED handbook and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, as established in PR #85 (SFCC-236 shared product card — atoms → molecules → organism, page-level mapper, `ui-kits/<name>Shared.ts`, theme registration, `desktop/`/`mobile/` e2e split), using: the **override** approach with copy-first for `product-item/` and `item-variant/` (mirrored base files exist), the **new-component** approach under `ui-kits/` for the drawer organism, quantity stepper, inline message, actions row, button group and empty state (no mirrored base file exists), **co-located `Zimm*` recipes** for all styling, and the **existing `--zimm-*` foundation untouched** — every colour and space value in this design already exists there.

---

## 2. Scale call — six branches, and how much loop each earns

> **⚠️ SUPERSEDED by §11 (Marcel, 2026-09-17): SINGLE PR, now 20 commits** (18 originally; the
> 3.5 stepper-wiring insertion on 2026-09-18 made it 19, the 4.6 cartDrawerContainer insertion on
> 2026-09-20 made it 20 — this line and the other plain "18"/"eighteen" mentions below went stale
> both times and were only just corrected; treat this number as the one to keep current, not
> re-derive from memory, if a further step ever gets inserted).
> Retained as the record of why the seams were drawn where they were. §3's file manifest and §4's
> steps remain valid verbatim — they regroup by commit instead of by branch. §5's per-step loop
> criteria remain valid; only the per-*branch* loop scaling is replaced.

### Six branches, not one PR and not seven

| # | Branch | Stories | Files | Why it is its own branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B0** | `fix/SFCC-11_cart-e2e-area` | — (infra) | 1 | `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is **Tier 1 CI/CD**. Bundling it into a feature PR drags `@tier-1-approvers` onto a feature review and breaches AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 (one protection tier per change). |
| **B1** | `feature/SFCC-315_cart-drawer` | 315 | ~7 | **Ships first and standalone.** SFCC-316 (Jhoan, same sprint, Ready for Development) composes into it. Anything that delays this branch delays someone else's active-sprint card. |
| **B2** | `feature/SFCC-270_cart-item-override` | 270 | ~14 | **The only Tier 2 code branch.** `product-item/` pulls `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. Keeping it alone means one squad-B reviewer sees one coherent override, not a 40-file cart feature. Also the only branch with a mandatory copy-first pause. |
| **B3** | `feature/SFCC-795-271_cart-item-states-stepper` | 795 + 271 | ~20 | 795 and 271 are the same pixels. §5.4: "795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states — one implementation, three cards' ACs." Splitting them means building the stepper twice. |
| **B4** | `feature/SFCC-250-272_max-qty-wishlist-actions` | 250 + 272 | ~16 | **Welded, per the settled decision.** Both land in one `onAuthSuccess` callback (merge → cap → wishlist resume). They cannot be reviewed or reverted independently. |
| **B5** | `feature/SFCC-275_cart-button-group` | 275 | ~6 | Independent of the cart-item chain. Can run in parallel with B2/B3 by a second pair of hands. |

Every branch is cut fresh from an updated `develop` (`origin/develop` head `71025f18`; local is 41 behind). Never from `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch`, which carries open PR #112.

**Order:** B0 ∥ B1 first → B2 (copy-first pause) → B3 → B4. B5 any time after B0. B4 depends on B3's stepper existing and on B1's drawer hosting the empty state.

### One Tier 2 touch you cannot design away

Every branch that adds a recipe must edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` to register it. That file is inside `overrides/app/theme/components/` → **Tier 2**, `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. The co-location relief in CODEOWNERS (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` → squads only, last-match-wins) covers the recipe *file* and not the registration *line*. So B1, B3, B4 and B5 each carry one Tier 2 approver for a one-line import + one key. Plan for it; do not be surprised by it at PR time.

### How much loop — scaled down deliberately

| Branch | Loop | Why |
|---|---|---|
| B0 | **None.** | A workflow allow-list. Verified by observing the next cart PR's `e2e_scope` output, not by a Tester. A loop here is theatre. |
| B1 | **Light** — Tester + Scorer on one pass. | Mostly reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already owns overlay, right placement, Escape, `finalFocusRef`, mobile full-height and scroll-lock. Two things are genuinely new (the 52px reserved band, the `xLarge` width fix) and both are assertable in one `.css.test.ts`. |
| B2 | **Full loop, but only on the copy-first pass.** | The risk here is not "does it look right", it is "did the override intercept and did the 11 downstream surfaces survive". After Marcel's verification the restyle is conventional. Dropping the second loop pass. |
| B3 | **Full loop.** | Largest surface: ~25 ACs including 11 accessibility, five stepper states, three error states, two breakpoint reflows. This is where a missed state ships. |
| B4 | **Full loop, and the only step that gets a second adversarial pass.** | Async state, an auth seam, an ordered callback, a loop guard and a render guard that must not race a mutation. Highest defect cost, lowest visibility in review. |
| B5 | **Light.** | 8 ACs, six presentational, one conditional render, one stubbed destination. A two-point story does not earn a full loop. |

**Explicitly dropped, and why:** no Playwright spec on B1 (nothing to drive it — see open question 7); no `.test.ts` on the four pure-presentation atoms/molecules whose only logic is prop interpolation (`testing.md`'s single-parent exemption — covered by the organism's `play`); no separate loop pass on B2's restyle commit. Anything more would be over-scaled machinery, which is a defect in a plan.

---

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`, owners read directly from `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`. Not from `.claude/registry/*.md`.

### B0 — e2e area

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.github/workflows/qa.yml` | modify | **Tier 1 CI/CD** | `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` |

> **BLOCKED.** Named explicitly in the brief, but owner approval is not confirmed. Per Hard Rule #2 the Implementer must either verify the authenticated `gh` login is in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (`gh api user --jq .login`, then the team membership call) or stop and get a named approving review before touching it. Do not start B0 on an unverified session.

Add a `cart` group to `detect-changes`'s allow-lists covering `overrides/app/pages/cart/**`, `overrides/app/components/product-item/**`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/**`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*/**`, `e2e/tests/zimm/cart/**`, `e2e/features/cart/**`. Note `e2e_homepage` is currently the **only** area group in the file — `testing.md`'s longer tag list is aspirational, so `cart` is the second, not the eighth.

### B1 — SFCC-315

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.test.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/index.stories.tsx` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.ts` | create | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmCartDrawer/zimmCartDrawer.css.test.ts` | create | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.ts` | **modify** | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` | modify | Tier 3 | same |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | modify | **Tier 2** | `@tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` |

### B2 — SFCC-270 (copy-first)

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/product-item/index.tsx` | create (copy of base `index.jsx`) | **Tier 2** | `@pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers` |
| `overrides/app/components/product-item/bonus-product-quantity.tsx` | create (copy) | **Tier 2** | same |
| `overrides/app/components/product-item/product-quantity-picker.tsx` | create (copy) | **Tier 2** | same |
| `overrides/app/components/product-item/product-item.css.ts` | create | Tier 3 (`**/*.css.ts`) | `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` |

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

**Changes.** New organism at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/`, wrapping `ZimmDrawer` with `size="xLarge"`. Props only — `isOpen`, `onClose`, `itemCount`, `finalFocusRef`, `children`, plus a `messages` slot and a `footer` slot (the footer slot is what hosts SFCC-275's button group until SFCC-816 lands). Recipe `ZimmCartDrawer` with parts for the messages band, the content container, and the two-column/one-column grid.

Header title: `"BAG • {count}"` via `ZimmDrawer`'s existing `title` prop (AC1). Empty: `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` — **header text only**; the empty *body* is SFCC-277's and arrives in B4 as a slotted component.

### B3 — SFCC-795 + 271, states and stepper

#### Step 3.1 — `ZimmQuantityStepper` molecule

**Changes.** New molecule composing two `ZimmButton`s at `size="icon"` around a value display. Gap **8px (`xs`)** per §11.11(1) — design showed a 12px gap around a 12px glyph with no touch target; we apply the system's 24px `minW`/`minH` (ZimmButton `icon` already is `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), which adds 6px invisible padding each side, so 8px yields 14px apparent. Annotate exactly that, citing WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 and the Figma node literally named `touchTarget` at 24.

Disabled glyphs use `OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4` from `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared.ts` — Figma ships separate greyed SVGs; we use opacity. One constant, one file, read by both the recipe and the tests.

**Pass criteria — every state named, because a state absent here is absent from the Tester's brief and the Scorer's gate:**
1. Quantity 1: `−` is `disabled`, carries `aria-disabled` or the native attribute, renders at 0.4 opacity; clicking it does nothing and quantity stays 1 (AC3).
2. Quantity > 1: both enabled; `−` decrements by exactly 1; `+` increments by exactly 1 (ACs 1, 2).
3. Quantity at max: `+` disabled and greyed, `−` still enabled (795 stepper group).
4. Fully OOS or unavailable: **both** disabled and greyed (795 stepper group).
5. **Hover, focus-visible and active** are inherited from `ZimmButton`'s `icon` variant, which already carries `_hover`/`_focusVisible`/`_active`/`_disabled`. Assert in the recipe test that the focus-visible ring's resolved value is **not identical to the default state** — an invisible focus state is a WCAG 2.4.7 failure and is the exact bug `zimmButton.css.ts` records having already shipped once. Figma supplies no hover/focus node for the stepper; inheritance is the resolution, annotated at the point of use. Do not invent a value.
6. Each button has an `aria-label` (`IconButton` renders no visible text — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`).
7. Resolved target size of each control is ≥24×24 CSS px, asserted from the recipe, not measured in a browser.
8. `index.stories.tsx` has a `play` covering increment, decrement, and the disabled-at-1 boundary.

#### Step 3.2 — `ZimmInlineMessage` atom + error/warning states

**Changes.** New atom, variant-driven: `error` (`status.error`) / `warning` (`text.muted`). It sits **between the stepper and the actions row**, full width, `textStyle="caption"` with weight overridden to regular per gate #13. **Presentation only.** OOS / partial OOS triggering is SFCC-282 and Unavailable is SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Hazel's. Build prop-driven with stories; do not wire detection logic.

Copy, verbatim from Figma: fully OOS **"This item is unavailable"**; partial OOS **"Quantity unavailable in this size"**; max quantity **"Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size"**.

Per gate #4, max-quantity renders as the **warning** variant (grey, `text.muted`), not error — the design and SFCC-250 AC4 agree; CAI-017's word "error" means user-facing feedback, not the severity tier. Annotate that reconciliation inline.

Per gate #9, **there is no low-stock variant** — CAI-030 forbids low-stock messaging at cart level. Do not add one.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Stories: `Error`, `Warning`, plus one per copy string above. Each renders the exact copy.
2. `error` resolves to `var(--zimm-color-status-error)`; `warning` to `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`. Both asserted in the recipe test against the token var, not a hex.
3. The organism recipe test asserts Item Details gap is the 12px token by default and the 16px token in the error state.
4. Message renders in DOM order **between** stepper and actions.
5. No `#9c0000`, `#969696` or any hex literal in either file — `npm run audit:tokens` clean.
6. No low-stock variant exists in the component's variant union.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

<example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

578	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

580	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
581	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
582	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
583	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
584	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
585	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
586	
587	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
588	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
589	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
590	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
591	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
592	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
593	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
594	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
595	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
596	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
597	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
598	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
599	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
600	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
601	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
602	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
603	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
604	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
605	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
606	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
607	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
608	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
609	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
610	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
611	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
612	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
613	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
614	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
615	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
616	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
617	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
618	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
619	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
620	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
621	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
622	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
623	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
624	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
625	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
626	9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
627	   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
628	   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
629	   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
630	   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
631	   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
632	   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
633	   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
634	   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
635	   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
636	   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
637	   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
638	   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
639	   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
640	   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.

643	
644	These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.
645	
646	1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. 647	
648	2. **`overrides/app/components/item-variant/` has no CODEOWNERS entry and there is no catch-all.** Five files with an 11-surface blast radius would merge with **no required reviewer**. Adding the entry is a Tier 1 Governance change to `CODEOWNERS`, explicitly outside my scope. Your call: add it as a separate ticket first, or accept that the widest-reaching part of this change is ungoverned and compensate with a manually-requested reviewer on B2.
649	
650	3. **`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` is also ungoverned, and the merge call changes auth behaviour for three surfaces outside the cart** (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`). Not in `frozenFiles.md`, not in `protectedFiles.md`'s shared-hooks list, no CODEOWNERS entry. This is a second instance of #2 and arguably the more dangerous one. Does B4 need an explicitly requested reviewer, and does the cross-surface behaviour change need Hard Rule #10 scope confirmation from you before it is written?
651	
652	4. **`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist.** The settled decision says "use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not the base hook" — but that file is absent, and the path is listed in `protectedFiles.md` and routed in CODEOWNERS to `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. My recommendation: import the base hook at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` and wrap it in our own untiered `useCartMessages.ts`. That satisfies the decision's actual intent (one handler, SFCC-404 is a one-file swap), costs no Tier 2 review, and automatically picks up the override the day someone creates it. I have **not** applied this — the decision is yours to confirm.
653	
654	5. **The stepper's `+` and `−` are a mismatched pair.** `MinusIcon` is a Zimmermann/Figma icon in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`; `PlusIcon` is re-exported from the base template in `index.tsx`. 655	
656	6. **Apple Pay and Google Pay marks do not exist.** `zimm.tsx` has `ZimmAppleSignInIcon` and `ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` — sign-in marks, not Pay marks — and there is no `applePay`/`googlePay` asset anywhere in `overrides/app`. 657	
658	7. **Nothing opens the cart drawer, and no story owns the trigger.** See the closing line.
659

Base `pages/cart/index.jsx` exists, so the override rule would normally say copy-first it — but the session notes decided 315 is explicitly "not an override of base `pages/cart`". 661

I am instructed not to plan changes under `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`. Confirm the Implementer should run it, and on which branches.
663

665

Do you accept shipping 250 tested only against the fallback, or does 268 need reopening first?

Force a basket over the cap and confirm the render guard fires exactly once and no-ops while a mutation is in flight. Render with zero items and confirm `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty list. | One `ProductItem` per line, mapped not hand-built; render guard proven to run and to no-op under `useIsMutating()`, mirroring 4.2's own proof but for the real wiring; `secondaryActions` is a real `ZimmCartItemActions` on every item; empty state swaps in at zero items; `footer`/`messages` slots render `ZimmCartButtonGroup`/`useCartMessages` output; container owns no `isOpen`/`onClose` state itself; exactly one production `<ZimmCartDrawer` call site. |

---

## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.

## 6. Open questions

These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.

1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. Until B0 lands, every cart PR gets `e2e_scope: skip` and no PR-time E2E.

2. **`overrides/app/components/item-variant/` has no CODEOWNERS entry and there is no catch-all.** Five files with an 11-surface blast radius would merge with **no required reviewer**. Adding the entry is a Tier 1 Governance change to `CODEOWNERS`, explicitly outside my scope. Your call: add it as a separate ticket first, or accept that the widest-reaching part of this change is ungoverned and compensate with a manually-requested reviewer on B2.

3. **`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` is also ungoverned, and the merge call changes auth behaviour for three surfaces outside the cart** (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`). Not in `frozenFiles.md`, not in `protectedFiles.md`'s shared-hooks list, no CODEOWNERS entry. This is a second instance of #2 and arguably the more dangerous one. Does B4 need an explicitly requested reviewer, and does the cross-surface behaviour change need Hard Rule #10 scope confirmation from you before it is written?

4. **`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist.** The settled decision says "use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not the base hook" — but that file is absent, and the path is listed in `protectedFiles.md` and routed in CODEOWNERS to `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. So honouring the decision literally means **creating a Tier 2 shared hook** this bundle has not budgeted a review for. My recommendation: import the base hook at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` and wrap it in our own untiered `useCartMessages.ts`. That satisfies the decision's actual intent (one handler, SFCC-404 is a one-file swap), costs no Tier 2 review, and automatically picks up the override the day someone creates it. I have **not** applied this — the decision is yours to confirm.

5. **The stepper's `+` and `−` are a mismatched pair.** `MinusIcon` is a Zimmermann/Figma icon in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`; `PlusIcon` is re-exported from the base template in `index.tsx`. That file's own comments show the established pattern of migrating an icon into `zimm.tsx` when the base glyph is wrong (`CloseIcon`: "off-centre glyph within its viewBox"; the chevrons: filled vs stroked). AGENTS.md is explicit: if a required icon is missing from the overrides set, **ask — do not substitute a visually different one**. Is the base `PlusIcon` acceptable against Figma's `Icon_plus`, or does it need adding to `zimm.tsx`?

6. **Apple Pay and Google Pay marks do not exist.** `zimm.tsx` has `ZimmAppleSignInIcon` and `ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` — sign-in marks, not Pay marks — and there is no `applePay`/`googlePay` asset anywhere in `overrides/app`. Both are brand-licensed artwork with usage rules. SFCC-275 AC1 requires 48×24 logos. Same AGENTS.md rule applies: ask, do not substitute. This is the only part of B5 that cannot pass.

7. **Nothing opens the cart drawer, and no story owns the trigger.** See the closing line.

8. **Container placement needs your confirmation.** SFCC-271's mutations and SFCC-250's guards need something that owns `useCurrentBasket()`, and `components.md` forbids data-fetching in anything under `overrides/app/components/`. Base `pages/cart/index.jsx` exists, so the override rule would normally say copy-first it — but the session notes decided 315 is explicitly "not an override of base `pages/cart`". My plan threads this by creating a **new custom file** at `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (a path CODEOWNERS already routes to `@pwa-squad-a`, Tier 3), leaving base `pages/cart/index.jsx` untouched and still serving `/cart` as today — a sibling file named anything other than `index` does not shadow the base page. Confirm that, or tell me to copy-first the page instead (which adds `index.jsx` + up to 13 partials to B2's scope).

9. **Registry regeneration sits inside my no-plan scope.** PR #85's shape includes `npm run generate:registry`, which writes `.claude/registry/{components,hooks,pages,routes,utils}.md`. I am instructed not to plan changes under `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`. It is a derived artefact that `postinstall` rewrites anyway, and `.claude/registry/` is **not** routed in CODEOWNERS (only `.claude/rules/` and `.claude/settings.json` are). Confirm the Implementer should run it, and on which branches.

10. **SFCC-318's existence is unconfirmed.** Listed in SFCC-315's description as a dependent, but not returned by the Jira key search. If it is real and someone is waiting on B1, that changes B1's urgency.

11. **SFCC-250 is not end-to-end verifiable this sprint.** Gate findings #1/#2: the TSD for SFCC-268 is `v0.1 Draft` with Technical Lead sign-off Pending, its own template says a TSD is not approved for implementation until signed, the live dev probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product — and Jira nonetheless has SFCC-268 as Ready for SIT. Do you accept shipping 250 tested only against the fallback, or does 268 need reopening first?

251	// default overrides the textStyle-derived value. Fix: set `fontSize` explicitly here using
252	// the zimm CSS var so it overwrites the leaked default and the final rendered size matches
253	// typography.ts (button = 14px, buttonSm = 12px).
254	const sizes = {
255	  lg: {
256	    h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg)', // 52px — confirmed by Figma + Handover
257	    minW: BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG, // 80px — Figma --alias-size-action-width-min, pending token
258	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg)', // 32px — confirmed by Figma + Handover
259	    // fontSize / fontWeight / lineHeight explicitly set to override Chakra's deep-merged
260	    // Button.sizes.lg defaults (fontSize:'lg'=1.125rem, fontWeight:'semibold'=600,
261	    // lineHeight:'1.2') — same issue as the baseStyle fontWeight: these leak through
262	    // extendTheme's deep-merge even when textStyle sets the correct values.
263	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)', // 14px
264	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
265	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs)', // 16px
266	    textStyle: 'button',
267	  },
268	  sm: {
269	    h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-md)', // 40px — confirmed by Figma 901:2897
270	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-md)', // 20px — confirmed by Figma 901:2897
271	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)', // 12px
272	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)', // 500
273	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)', // 18px
274	    textStyle: 'buttonSm',
275	  },
276	  // Social button responsive size. Figma confirms height/typography step at the md
277	  // breakpoint, but horizontal padding is 32px at every breakpoint — NOT responsive.
278	  // Corrected 2026-09: the previous version of this comment claimed padding also stepped
279	  // down to 20px on mobile ("Figma confirms all three variants"); live Figma inspection
280	  // showed that was wrong — px was always meant to be var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg).
281	  // Mobile: 40px h, 32px px, buttonSm (12px/500/18px lh)
282	  // Desktop (md+): 52px h, 32px px, button (14px/500/16px lh)
283	  // Also used by primary/secondary buttons inside the auth drawer (size="adaptive")
284	  // via ZimmButton's adaptive→social size mapping — same tokens, different variant colours.
285	  social: {
286	    // h (explicit fixed height) guarantees the flex container has a known height so
287	    // align-items:center always has space to distribute. minH alone can resolve to nothing
288	    // if the CSS variable hasn't loaded, leaving the button at content height with no
289	    // centering space. whiteSpace:normal (from the social variant) still allows text wrapping
290	    // if the label needs it; overflow:clip (from baseStyle) handles any rare overflow.
291	    h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-md)',
292	    // Constant across breakpoints — see the comment above this size. Not var(--...-h-md)
293	    // (20px): that's the mobile action-height tier's own padding token, but this button's
294	    // horizontal padding was never meant to shrink with it.
295	    px: 'var(--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg)',
296	    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)',
297	    fontWeight: 'var(--zimm-font-weight-medium)',
298	    lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)',
299	    textStyle: 'buttonSm',
300	    [`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`]: {
301	      h: 'var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg)',
302	      fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)',
303	      lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs)',
304	      textStyle: 'button',
305	    },
306	  },
307	  // WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target size. SFCC-55's accessibility note names this
308	  // control specifically ("the minimum size of that email sign up button").
309	  //
310	  // minW/minH, NOT padding: Chakra's IconButton hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a *style prop*, and
311	  // style props merge after __css, so any p/px/py declared here is silently discarded. The
312	  // previous `p: 'xs'` read as a 32px target and rendered 16x16 — the icon's own boxSize.
313	  //
314	  // var, not 'xl': min-width/height resolve through theme.sizes (xl = 36rem = 576px), not
315	  // theme.space. Same rule and same token as clearButton in zimmTextInput.ts, which is the
316	  // sibling control in the same trailing slot.
317	  icon: {
318	    h: 'auto',
319	    minW: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
320	    minH: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
321	  },
322	};
323	
324	export const Button = defineStyleConfig({
325	  baseStyle,
326	  variants,
327	  sizes,
328	  defaultProps: {
329	    variant: 'primary',
330	    size: 'lg',
331	  },
332	});
333	
334	// Figma: every button label carries text-box-trim:trim-both + text-box-edge:cap_alphabetic
335	// to strip Futura Round's metric whitespace above cap-height and below the alphabetic
336	// baseline so uppercase glyphs sit at the true visual centre.
337	export const ZimmButtonLabel = defineStyleConfig({
338	  baseStyle: {
339	    flexShrink: 0,
340	    textBoxTrim: 'trim-both',
341	    textBoxEdge: 'cap alphabetic',
342	  },
343	});
344

1	// Icon sizes — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026 (Handover tokens.md § Icon Sizes)
2	//
3	// Deliberately NOT registered as `theme.sizes`. Chakra's `sizes.lg` is 32rem and
4	// backs every `w`/`h`/`boxSize` token across the base retail-react-app, so
5	// remapping these names would resize base components. Import these constants
6	// directly instead — the same pattern component overrides already use for
7	// FONT_MEDIUM: `<Icon boxSize={iconSizes.lg} />`.
8	export const iconSizes = {
9	  xl: '24px',
10	  lg: '20px',
11	  md: '16px',
12	  sm: '12px',
13	} as const;
14	
15	// Action (button) sizing — source: Handover tokens/spacing.css (--zimm-size-action-*).
16	// The CSS-var twins already exist in zimmTokens.ts. zimmButton.css.ts (the single source
17	// of truth for actual button styling) uses var(--zimm-size-action-height-lg/md) directly,
18	// which resolves to these Figma-confirmed values (52px / 40px).
19	export const actionSizes = {
20	  height: {
21	    lg: '52px',
22	    md: '40px',
23	  },
24	  paddingX: {
25	    lg: '32px',
26	    md: '20px',
27	  },
28	  gap: '16px',
29	} as const;
30	
31	// Mega-menu sizing — source: Zimmermann Design System 2026, Figma node 40002429:7215
32	// (two-column "Expanded Menu" Nav Group, confirmed against SFCC-883).
33	export const megaMenuSizes = {
34	  twoColumnMaxWidth: '700px',
35	} as const;

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
4	import { Center, Stack, Text, Button } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
5	import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
6	
7	const ZIMM_CART_EMPTY_STATE_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartEmptyState';
8	
9	const messages = defineMessages({
10	  // Deliberately generic -- see this file's own "Placeholder body" note below for why the real
11	  // Figma copy (a specific AU phone number, AU opening hours, and a support email) is not shipped
12	  // here. Echoes the real copy's own opening phrase ("If you'd like some help...") since that
13	  // sentence starter carries no region-specific detail of its own to get wrong.
14	  body: {
15	    id: 'zimm_cart_empty_state.body',
16	    defaultMessage: "If you'd like some help, please get in touch with our Client Services team.",
17	  },
18	  continueShopping: {
19	    id: 'zimm_cart_empty_state.cta.continue_shopping',
20	    defaultMessage: 'Continue Shopping',
21	  },
22	});
23	
24	/**
25	 * Organism -- SFCC-272 AC2 ("removing the last item shows the empty state 'as per SFCC-277'") /
26	 * SFCC-11 plan step 4.5. A **discrete, swappable placeholder** for the cart drawer's empty-bag
27	 * body: SFCC-277 (a separate, not-yet-groomed card, out of this epic's 7-card bundle) owns the
28	 * real content and replaces this file's contents wholesale -- building it as its own component
29	 * rather than inline JSX in `ZimmCartDrawer` is what makes that a swap in one file
30	 * (`.claude/session-notes.md` §4 SFCC-272 decision "AC2 (empty state...): ... Build it as a
31	 * discrete component, not inline JSX in the drawer, so 277 is a swap in one file").
32	 *
33	 * **No heading in this component.** "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" is SFCC-315 AC2's own, already-shipped
34	 * header text (`zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx`'s `title = itemCount === 0 ? 'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' : ...`,
35	 * rendered by `ZimmDrawer`'s own title slot) -- session-notes.md §11.7 confirms this split
36	 * explicitly ("'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' is in the header, not the body"). This component is body-only.
37	 *
38	 * **Structure from the `pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` precedent** (`EmptyRecentlyViewed`, itself a
39	 * disclosed, undesigned port of base SFCC's `EmptyCart`,
40	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`):
41	 * `Box > Center > Stack`, a `Button as={Link}` CTA using the **base SFCC `Link`** (not
42	 * `ZimmLink` -- so the href gets this storefront's real multi-site prefixing via
43	 * `use-multi-site.js`'s `buildUrl`, called internally by that `Link`), `useIntl` called directly
44	 * in this leaf under the Context-backed exception `.claude/rules/components.md` > Composition
45	 * documents for `useIntl`/`useUiCopy` specifically. Visuals (colour/type/spacing tokens) come from
46	 * SFCC-315's EMPTY BAG Figma nodes (session-notes.md §11.7) instead of that precedent's own
47	 * autonomous token choices -- that file's own docblock discloses those as an unbacked judgement
48	 * call made with no design at all; this state has one.
49	 *
50	 * **The CTA button is a structural decision from the precedent, not a Figma- or AC-sourced
51	 * requirement -- disclosed, not silently assumed.** Checked directly before building:
52	 * `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/figma-reference/empty-bag.md` (live Figma pull, all
53	 * three breakpoints) states plainly "there is no 'continue shopping' / 'browse' button or any
54	 * call-to-action in this Figma state at all," and flags checking SFCC-272's actual AC text before
55	 * assuming one is expected. That AC text (session-notes.md line 421-422, pulled from
56	 * `customfield_10231`) reads only "removing the last item shows the empty state 'as per
57	 * SFCC-277'" -- no CTA of any kind. The CTA renders here anyway because `plan.md` step 4.5's own
58	 * "Changes" text mandates taking **structure** from the `recentlyViewed`/`EmptyCart` precedent
59	 * regardless of what the literal Figma mockup omits (a shopper needs a way out of an empty
60	 * drawer) -- a plan-level call, not something either source document asked for on its own.
61	 *
62	 * **No `isRegistered` branching -- checked, not assumed.** The precedent's own body copy and CTA
63	 * set both branch on `isRegistered` (a guest additionally sees "Sign In," matching base
64	 * `EmptyCart`'s identical split). Before copying that here, checked: session-notes.md §11.7 (the
65	 * real Figma content list for this exact state) names exactly one body message with no
66	 * guest/registered variant; §11.9/§11.10 (the design-issues and resolved-items lists) raise the
67	 * hardcoded-AU-contact-details question but never an auth-state question; the actual SFCC-272 AC
68	 * text above says nothing about auth state either (the empty-state AC is a single sentence
69	 * deferring entirely to SFCC-277). With no source anywhere calling for a split, and the body
70	 * itself already a generic placeholder standing in for SFCC-277's real copy, adding an invented
71	 * `isRegistered` branch on top would be a second layer of invention with nothing backing it --
72	 * so this component takes no props at all and renders one body message and one CTA regardless of
73	 * auth state. Flagged here for Marcel to override if SFCC-277's own grooming later says otherwise.
74	 *
75	 * **Placeholder body -- deliberately generic, no AU-specific contact details.** The real Figma
76	 * copy (session-notes.md §11.7) is "If you'd like some help, speak to one of our Client Services
77	 * Advisors at: / +61 1800 738 895 / Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM / or
78	 * clientservices@zimmermann.com" -- hardcoded to the AU storefront in the design, with no AC
79	 * covering how it should vary across the other 7 storefronts / 6 regions. Marcel settled
80	 * (session-notes.md §11.9, 2026-09-16) that this is explicitly not this build's problem: "we ship
81	 * a placeholder empty state only; the real one is SFCC-277's... the question carries to SFCC-277
82	 * -- flag on 277 at grooming." The copy above echoes only the real line's opening phrase (which
83	 * names no region-specific detail) and invites contact with no number, hours, or email at all.
84	 *
85	 * **No outer vertical padding set.** There is no confirmed Figma value for the vertical space
86	 * around this block once nested in the drawer body, and `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
87	 * ("Component-local tokens") is explicit for exactly this situation: "leave it inherited... rather
88	 * than inventing a number." (`pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own `EmptyRecentlyViewed` uses
89	 * `paddingY="var(--zimm-scale-4xl)"` here, but that value is itself disclosed in that file as an
90	 * unconfirmed autonomous guess -- reusing it would just be borrowing one unverified number into a
91	 * second, unrelated component rather than independently confirming it, which
92	 * `.claude/rules/typescript.md`-adjacent house discipline on reused numbers argues against.)
93	 * Horizontal gutter needs no equivalent decision: `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own `body` part already
94	 * applies `paddingInline` at every breakpoint (`zimmCartDrawer.css.ts`), so this component
95	 * inherits it once nested there rather than declaring a second, competing value.
96	 *
97	 * **Recipe (`zimmCartEmptyState.css.ts`) owns exactly one thing:** making this component's root
98	 * span both of `ZimmCartDrawer`'s desktop grid tracks (session-notes.md §11.7 / plan.md step 4.5:
99	 * "two columns collapse to one") instead of being confined to the 360px items column with 430px
100	 * of dead space beside it. See that file's own docblock for the full mechanism, and this step's
101	 * own report for how far that was verified live vs. deferred to step 4.6 (the container that
102	 * will actually nest this component inside the real drawer at zero items -- not built yet;
103	 * `ZimmCartDrawer` today still renders its own hardcoded interim placeholder text at
104	 * `itemCount === 0`, not `children`, so a real nested render of this component doesn't exist
105	 * until that step wires the swap).
106	 *
107	 * No props -- there is nothing for a caller to configure in a placeholder standing in for a card
108	 * that hasn't been groomed yet. SFCC-277 is expected to need real ones (at minimum, per-storefront
109	 * contact details) when it replaces this file's contents.
110	 */
111	export const ZimmCartEmptyState = () => {
112	  const intl = useIntl();
113	  const styles = useStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_EMPTY_STATE_RECIPE);
114	
115	  return (
116	    <chakra.div __css={styles} data-testid="zimm-cart-empty-state">
117	      <Center>
118	        <Stack spacing="var(--zimm-scale-xl)" textAlign="center">
119	          {/* var(--zimm-scale-xl) = 24px -- session-notes.md §11.10(4): "25px raw value --
120	              DECIDED (Marcel): implement 24px ... Applies to ... the empty-bag paragraph
121	              spacing." Same snap-to-nearest-token convention as
122	              zimmCartItemActions.css.ts's own `gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // Figma: 25px,
123	              snapped to the nearest token (24px)` comment. */}
124	          <Text textStyle="body1" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
125	            {intl.formatMessage(messages.body)}
126	          </Text>
127	          <Button as={Link} href="/" variant="primary" width={{ base: 'full', sm: 'auto' }} alignSelf="center">
128	            {intl.formatMessage(messages.continueShopping)}
129	          </Button>
130	        </Stack>
131	      </Center>
132	    </chakra.div>
133	  );
134	};
135	
136	// --- Decision log -------------------------------------------------------------------------
137	// 1. No isRegistered branching (body copy or CTA) -- checked session-notes.md §§11.7/11.9/11.10
138	//    and SFCC-272's actual pulled AC text; none call for a split. See this file's own docblock
139	//    for the full reasoning. Ready for Marcel to override if SFCC-277's grooming disagrees.
140	// 2. CTA button included despite neither Figma (figma-reference/empty-bag.md) nor SFCC-272's AC
141	//    text showing/requesting one -- plan.md step 4.5's own "Changes" text mandates it via the
142	//    recentlyViewed/EmptyCart structural precedent. Disclosed, not silently assumed.
143	// 3. Body copy is generic placeholder prose, not the real Figma contact copy -- Marcel's own
144	//    2026-09-16 decision (session-notes.md §11.9), carried forward to SFCC-277's grooming.
145	// 4. No outer vertical padding -- no confirmed Figma value; left unset per
146	//    overrideStyling.md's "leave it inherited... rather than inventing a number," rather than
147	//    reusing recentlyViewed's own already-disclosed-as-unconfirmed 64px guess.
148	// 5. Text alignment (centred) is inherited from the mandated Box > Center > Stack precedent
149	//    structure, not independently confirmed against Figma (the empty-bag.md pull does not state
150	//    an alignment for the description text block either way). Two separate mechanisms, not one:
151	//    the outer Stack's own `textAlign="center"` centres the text node, and the Button's own
152	//    `alignSelf="center"` is what actually centres it as a flex item within that Stack --
153	//    `textAlign` alone does not position a flex child.
154

495	comment on the card**, because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to
496	know two items is intended rather than a bug.
497	
498	**Deliberate boundary, recorded so it isn't mistaken for an oversight:** per-line enforcement means
499	a SKU split across two lines can total more than 3 without either line hitting max. That case only
500	arises from the merge splitting a line, which is what AC5 exists to catch. In that same edge case the
501	PDP (which sums per SKU) and the cart (per line) apply different rules.
502	
503	### SFCC-275 — Button Group · 8 ACs · 6 as-scoped, 2 to the boundary
504	
505	ACs: domestic → Checkout CTA (primary, full-width black) then Apple Pay Express (outlined) then
506	Google Pay Express (outlined), in that fixed order; international → express buttons not displayed and
507	content above the CTA shifts up with no white gap; error in cart → all three remain **visually
508	enabled** but blocked at backend level; errors resolved → block removed; domestic, any auth status →
509	straight to checkout; international **guest** → intermediate login page (SFCC-880); international
510	**authenticated** → straight to Global-e (SFCC-63); responsive per Figma.
511	
512	- **Not blocked on SFCC-816.** The card says the group sits *within* the cart summary component —
513	  a location, not a dependency. Build standalone with its own story and drop it in later.
514	- **Reuse:** `ZimmButton`'s `primary` and `secondary` (outlined) variants cover AC1 with no atom gap.
515	  The domestic/international branch is a `checkoutOwner` read (§2.12), whose own doc comment directs
516	  exactly this use.
517	- **ACs 3/4: deliver 275's half only** — buttons render enabled during error states. Backend blocking
518	  is not in a UI story, and the ACs specify **no shopper-facing feedback** for a click that does
519	  nothing. Flag the feedback gap; don't invent copy.
520	- **ACs 6/7: build the branch, stub the destination.** SFCC-880 is To Do, **unassigned, no sprint**;
521	  Global-e is "Not started" in `projectState.md` with PRC-43/PRC-46 open. Leaving international on the
522	  base `/checkout` path is the **current** behaviour (§2.13), so the stub is a no-op, not a regression.
523	- **SFCC-309 overlap, resolved.** 309's description claims the express buttons' *"button rendering,
524	  display logic"* and scopes 275 to *"the Checkout CTA layout"* — contradicting 275's own three-button
525	  scope. But 309 is a **self-declared placeholder** with no ACs (`customfield_10231` is null), no
526	  sprint, unassigned. **Specified beats placeholder.** The seam that all three cards support is
527	  **region-based vs device-based**: 275 owns presentation + the region hide (`checkoutOwner`);
528	  309/383/384 own device and browser eligibility, payment flows, tokenisation and order placement.
529	- **Where it renders — DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): SFCC-315 hosts the button group**, with
530	  SFCC-816 taking over hosting when it lands. Otherwise the drawer ships with no way to check out.
531	- AC8 needs the Figma, which has not been opened yet.
532	- 309 also carries an unanswered question that does not block 275: *"confirm which storefronts
533	  support G Pay and Apple Pay."*
534	
535	---
536	
537	## 5. Cross-story interactions
538	
539	1. **250 + 272 share one callback.** Merge → cap → wishlist resume lands both stories in the same
540	   function, so they cannot be staged, reviewed or reverted independently. Build as one PR at that
541	   seam. Keep merge-and-cap in its own function so the logic stays separable.
542	2. **The §2.5 defect gates both.** No merge → nothing for AC5 to cap, and no cart item left for
543	   272's AC8 to move to the wishlist.
544	3. **275's AC3 vs 250's AC4.** 275 lists "quantity error requiring customer action" as a blocking
545	   condition; 250 says max-quantity explicitly does **not** block checkout. They reconcile only if
546	   max-qty is not such an error — which 250 asserts. Confirm, since both cards specify the same
547	   button's state.
548	4. **795 subsumes 270, 271 and 250's UI states.** One implementation, three cards' ACs.
549	
550	---
551	
552	## 6. Prerequisite — do this first
553	
554	**Verify then file the passwordless-merge defect (§2.5).**
555	1. Prove it live: guest adds an item → opens the cart → signs in with the email code → check whether
556	   the item survives. (A finding isn't real until it has been made to fail on purpose.)
557	2. File against the wishlist auth drawer lineage (SFCC-742 / SFCC-926), **not** against 250 or 272 —
558	   it is pre-existing.
559	3. Build the merge as step 1 of the 250/272 work regardless, because both cards need it.
560	
561	---
562	
563	## 7. Jira comments to post — **DEFERRED UNTIL AFTER THE BUILD** (Marcel, 2026-09-16)
564	
565	All of §7 and §8, plus filing/verifying the §6 defect, happen **after** the build, not before.
566	**Exception — §6's merge call is still step 1 of the 250/272 build work**, because 250's AC5 has
567	nothing to cap without it and 272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. Only the *ticket* and the
568	*live verification* are deferred; the code is in scope.
569	
570	(no AC edits — PO-approved cards are not edited)
571	
572	- **SFCC-250** — `sum_quantities` accepted, including that it changes every merge; ACs 3 and 8's
573	  page-level banner deferred to SFCC-404; per-line (not per-SKU) enforcement and the boundary that
574	  follows from it.
575	- **SFCC-272** — message behaviour and copy delivered via an interim toast, surface deferred to
576	  SFCC-404; AC7 uses the existing wishlist auth drawer rather than a page redirect, per `cart.md` §2
577	  CAI-008; AC2's empty state built simply now, refined by SFCC-277.
578	- **SFCC-268** — its "BM Config" title does not match the sandbox; no max-order-quantity setting or
579	  custom attribute exists, so the frontend constant is the implementation (§2.1).
580	- **SFCC-309** — 275 delivers the button presentation and the region-based hide; 309's grooming
581	  should start from device/browser behaviour only.
582	- **SFCC-795** — the 44×44px AC is annotated against the existing 24px WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 target
583	  size and added to the UI designer's open list; note the AC labels a 2.1 AAA value as 2.1 AA.

3	 * currency truth (countries.generated.ts, regenerate via
4	 * `npm run sync:regional-config`) with a hand-maintained overlay for the
5	 * fields Business Manager/SCAPI has no concept of: shipping country,
6	 * checkout ownership, and boutique region grouping.
7	 *
8	 * Used by: URL routing, IP-detection prompt, checkout redirect logic,
9	 * boutique location filtering, hreflang generation.
10	 *
11	 * When adding a country:
12	 *   1. Add it to config/sites.overlay.js (and e2e/fixtures/site.overlay.js
13	 *      if it needs e2e coverage), then run `npm run sync:regional-config`.
14	 *   2. Add its business-logic overlay entry below (shippingCountry,
15	 *      checkoutOwner, globalEPricing, boutiqueRegion).
16	 *   3. Ensure a compiled translation exists in overrides/app/static/translations/compiled/.
17	 *
18	 * Unresolved — do not hard-code:

20	 *   - Denmark routing
21	 *   - China
22	 */

25

27	 * Who owns checkout for this site's domestic path.
28	 * For HK and ME, Global-e always owns checkout AND pricing from PDP onward.
29	 * For AU, US, GB, EU: SFCC owns domestic paths; Global-e takes over when the

46	   * Checkout owner for this site's domestic path.

import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the "Remove" / "Move to Wishlist" action-links row (SFCC-270 AC8, SFCC-272). Single
 * style, no parts: both links get their full visual treatment from `ZimmLink`'s own recipe
 * (`zimmLink.css.ts`, size `small` — capitalize, 12px/500/14px-lh, plus that recipe's own
 * hover/focus-visible states); this recipe only owns the row's own layout, matching
 * `zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts`'s own single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` — Figma specifies 25px (§11.10(4) of the SFCC-11 plan); no `--zimm-scale-*` step lands on
 * 25 (foundation/spacing.ts's steps go ...m:16px, l:20px, xl:24px, 2xl:32px... — confirmed no
 * 25px entry), so this snaps to the nearest existing token, 24px (`xl`), and records the raw
 * design value here rather than typing an unregistered one-off literal.
 *
 * `color` on each link is NOT set here: `ZimmLink`'s own `link.default` alias
 * (`foundation/colour.ts:87`, `grey[900]`) and `foundation/colour.ts:61`'s `text.default` (also
 * `grey[900]`) are the same primitive, so plain `<ZimmLink>` already renders the colour this
 * component's own spec calls for — adding a second, competing colour declaration here would be
 * exactly the anti-pattern `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface
 * per component type" section warns against (a value that can drift from the atom's own recipe
 * over time instead of there being only one place it's declared).
 */
export const ZimmCartItemActions = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // Figma: 25px, snapped to the nearest token (24px)
  },
});

51	  /**
52	   * When true, Global-e owns pricing, currency, and tax display from PDP
53	   * onward — do not render SFCC prices on these paths.
54	   */
55	  globalEPricing: boolean;
56	  /** Key used to filter boutique locations for this region */
57	  boutiqueRegion: string;
58	};
59	
60	type CountryOverlayEntry = Pick<
61	  CountryConfig,
62	  'shippingCountry' | 'checkoutOwner' | 'globalEPricing' | 'boutiqueRegion'
63	>;
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hand-maintained business/geo data, keyed the same way as
67	 * countries.generated.ts (URL slug; 'au' for the root/default site).
68	 *
69	 * 'en-ca' (US international) is defined here ready to go, but has no
70	 * matching entry in countries.generated.ts yet — it's excluded from the
71	 * final COUNTRIES export below until the ZimmermannUSIntl site is added to
72	 * config/sites.overlay.js (pending BM confirmation of the real site ID —
73	 * see .docs/planning/regionalConfigSyncPlan.md).
74	 */
75	const COUNTRY_OVERLAY: Record<string, CountryOverlayEntry> = {
76	  au: { shippingCountry: 'AU', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'australia' },
77	  us: { shippingCountry: 'US', checkoutOwner: 'hybrid', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' },
78	  'en-ca': { shippingCountry: 'CA', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'usa' }, // TBC — pending ZimmermannUSIntl
79	  uk: { shippingCountry: 'GB', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'uk' },
80	  'en-eu': { shippingCountry: 'DE', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
81	  'fr-eu': { shippingCountry: 'FR', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' },
82	  'it-eu': { shippingCountry: 'IT', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
83	  'es-eu': { shippingCountry: 'ES', checkoutOwner: 'sfcc', globalEPricing: false, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; shipping country resolved at checkout
84	  'en-ch': { shippingCountry: 'CH', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'europe' }, // placeholder; Global-e resolves shipping country
85	  hk: { shippingCountry: 'HK', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'hong-kong' },
86	  'en-ae': { shippingCountry: 'AE', checkoutOwner: 'global-e', globalEPricing: true, boutiqueRegion: 'middle-east' },
87	};
88	
89	/**
90	 * Keyed by urlSlug for O(1) lookup in routing/middleware.
91	 * AU is the exception: it has no URL prefix (root domain). Its key is 'au'
92	 * but urlSlug is '' — routing falls back to DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG when no
93	 * prefix is detected.
94	 */
95	// Fail loud, not silent, if BM/the sync script produced a slug with no
96	// matching business-logic overlay — that means someone added a site to
97	// config/sites.overlay.js and ran `npm run sync:regional-config` without
98	// adding the corresponding COUNTRY_OVERLAY entry above. The reverse case
99	// (an overlay entry with no generated data yet, e.g. 'en-ca' pending the
100	// US-split site ID) is intentional and handled by the filter below instead.
101	const missingOverlays = Object.keys(GENERATED_COUNTRIES).filter((slug) => !(slug in COUNTRY_OVERLAY));
102	if (missingOverlays.length) {
103	  throw new Error(
104	    `countries.ts: config/sites.overlay.js has a site for slug(s) '${missingOverlays.join(', ')}' with no ` +
105	      `matching COUNTRY_OVERLAY entry — add shippingCountry/checkoutOwner/globalEPricing/boutiqueRegion for it.`,
106	  );
107	}
108	
109	export const COUNTRIES: Record<string, CountryConfig> = Object.fromEntries(
110	  Object.entries(COUNTRY_OVERLAY)
111	    .filter(([slug]) => slug in GENERATED_COUNTRIES)
112	    .map(([slug, overlay]) => [
113	      slug,
114	      {
115	        urlSlug: slug === 'au' ? '' : slug,
116	        ...(GENERATED_COUNTRIES as Record<string, { sfccSiteId: string; locale: string; currency: string }>)[slug],
117	        ...overlay,
118	      },
119	    ]),

import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the cart drawer's Checkout / Apple Pay / Google Pay button stack (SFCC-275, SFCC-11
 * plan step 5.1). Single style, no parts: all three buttons get their full visual treatment from
 * `ZimmButton`'s own `primary`/`secondary` recipe (`zimmButton.css.ts`) — this recipe only owns
 * the group's own layout, matching `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` is `var(--zimm-size-action-gap)` (16px) — session-notes.md §11.5 confirms Figma's
 * `gap-[16px]` is literally `space/400`, and `foundation/sizes.ts`'s own comment on `actionSizes`
 * confirms this is the SAME action-sizing token `ZimmButton`'s own `lg` size (h52/px32) already
 * resolves through, not a second, independently-typed 16px value.
 *
 * No fixed `height`/`minHeight` here, deliberately — SFCC-11 plan step 5.1 AC2 ("no white gap"
 * when the international variant renders one child instead of three): a plain flexbox `gap`
 * naturally removes both a removed child's own height AND its adjacent gap when that child is
 * gone, with nothing here to compensate. Adding a fixed height would silently reintroduce exactly
 * the dead-space bug AC2 exists to prevent — see this recipe's own `index.test.tsx` assertion
 * that no `height`/`minHeight` key exists on this baseStyle.
 */
export const ZimmCartButtonGroup = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    width: '100%',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-size-action-gap)',
  },
});

 * the group's own layout, matching `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` is `var(--zimm-size-action-gap)` (16px) — session-notes.md §11.5 confirms Figma's
 * `gap-[16px]` is literally `space/400`, and `foundation/sizes.ts`'s own comment on `actionSizes`
 * confirms this is the SAME action-sizing token `ZimmButton`'s own `lg` size (h52/px32) already
 * resolves through, not a second, independently-typed 16px value.
 *
 * No fixed `height`/`minHeight` here, deliberately — SFCC-11 plan step 5.1 AC2 ("no white gap"
 * when the international variant renders one child instead of three): a plain flexbox `gap`
 * naturally removes both a removed child's own height AND its adjacent gap when that child is
 * gone, with nothing here to compensate. Adding a fixed height would silently reintroduce exactly
 * the dead-space bug AC2 exists to prevent — see this recipe's own `index.test.tsx` assertion
 * that no `height`/`minHeight` key exists on this baseStyle.
 */
export const ZimmCartButtonGroup = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    width: '100%',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-size-action-gap)',
  },
});

import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the cart drawer's Checkout / Apple Pay / Google Pay button stack (SFCC-275, SFCC-11
 * plan step 5.1). Single style, no parts: all three buttons get their full visual treatment from
 * `ZimmButton`'s own `primary`/`secondary` recipe (`zimmButton.css.ts`) — this recipe only owns
 * the group's own layout, matching `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`'s single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` is `var(--zimm-size-action-gap)` (16px) — session-notes.md §11.5 confirms Figma's
 * `gap-[16px]` is literally `space/400`, and `foundation/sizes.ts`'s own comment on `actionSizes`
 * confirms this is the SAME action-sizing token `ZimmButton`'s own `lg` size (h52/px32) already
 * resolves through, not a second, independently-typed 16px value.
 *
 * No fixed `height`/`minHeight` here, deliberately — SFCC-11 plan step 5.1 AC2 ("no white gap"
 * when the international variant renders one child instead of three): a plain flexbox `gap`
 * naturally removes both a removed child's own height AND its adjacent gap when that child is
 * gone, with nothing here to compensate. Adding a fixed height would silently reintroduce exactly
 * the dead-space bug AC2 exists to prevent — see this recipe's own `index.test.tsx` assertion
 * that no `height`/`minHeight` key exists on this baseStyle.
 */
export const ZimmCartButtonGroup = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    flexDirection: 'column',
    width: '100%',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-size-action-gap)',
  },
});
