input.message: ## Step 5.1 done: ZimmCartButtonGroup — build works, but the plan's own asset instructions were wrong about how this codebase's webpack actually handles SVGs. Fixed using an already-proven pattern, flagged loudly below. Branch confirmed `feature/SFCC-11_cart` (not develop/main) before touching anything. ### Files touched **Created:** - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx` - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.test.tsx` - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.stories.tsx` - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/zimmCartButtonGroup.css.ts` **Modified:** - `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — exactly a 2-line addition (1 import + 1 key), confirmed via `git diff --stat` (`2 insertions(+)`). **Not touched, verified:** - `overrides/app/assets/svg/apple-pay-logo.svg` / `google-pay-logo.svg` — only ever `Read`, never `Write`/`Edit`. Used as the source of truth for the inlined path data (see below), not modified. - `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — `git status --porcelain` on it returns nothing (pass criterion 7). --- ### The one thing that actually matters here: `` would have shipped invisible Pay logos **Consequence.** If I'd followed plan.md step 5.1 and its "(2) Apple Pay/Google Pay marks" section literally — `` — the Checkout button would look right and the Apple Pay / Google Pay buttons would render as **empty bordered boxes with no logo** in the real deployed app, dev and prod both. Every automated gate I'm required to run would still go green: Vitest has its own separate SVG transform (raw path string, harmless), and Storybook's own webpack config has a special carve-out that makes project SVGs resolve fine there too. Only the real app would be broken, and nothing in this loop would have caught it. **Mechanism, verified by reading the actual config, not assumed.** `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/config.js:186-190` applies `svg-sprite-loader` (server) / `ignore-loader` (client) to **every** `.svg` import, unscoped — `test: /\.svg$/` with no `include`/`exclude`, so it hits a brand-new file under `overrides/app/assets/svg/` exactly as hard as a base-package icon. This repo's own root `webpack.config.js` only re-exports that config with an unrelated Adyen chunk tweak — it adds no SVG override. `ZimmLogo` (`app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLogo/index.tsx`) already hit this and says so in its own docblock: *"Inlined because webpack svg-sprite-loader (server) + ignore-loader (client) prevent `` from resolving an SVG import to a URL."* Nobody connected that existing note to this step's asset instructions when the plan was written. **Fix.** I inlined both marks as JSX `` elements inside a `chakra.svg`, matching `ZimmLogo`'s exact established pattern — same technique, not a new one. I did **not** hand-redraw anything: I extracted the `d` attributes from the two committed SVG files and verified byte-for-byte equality programmatically (a Node script diffing all 5 `` values between the source files and my component — all 5 matched exactly, lengths 1957/127/1004/483/3057 chars). Fill is resolved via `useToken('colors', ['text.default'])` (grey[900]), same technique `ZimmLogo` uses for the same reason (`fill` needs a concrete value, not a `var()` string). The plan's explicit "do NOT add these to `zimm.tsx` via `createIcon`" instruction (a licensing/hand-transcription concern) still stands and isn't violated — I copied the real path data verbatim, I didn't redraw it. **This is disclosed, not silently decided** — it's the headline of this report, and it's in the component's own decision-log comment (item 1) with the same citation trail. --- ### Navigation-prop shape — no props at all, resolved internally (disclosed choice, per your brief's instruction to check precedent first) Checked both precedents your brief named: - `product-item`'s `secondaryActions`/`ZimmCartItemActions` shape: caller-supplied callback props (`onRemove`, `onMoveToWishlist`), because the *real mutation* is deliberately deferred to the not-yet-built container (step 4.6). - `zimmCartEmptyState`'s CTA: `Button as={Link}` using base SFCC `Link`/`Button` — but `ZimmButton` (which this step must use, per plan text) has no `as`/`href` prop at all, only `onClick`. Neither fits directly, because pass criterion 6 requires the domestic-vs-international **branch itself** to be provable from this component's own test file, before step 4.6 exists — there's no "real mutation" to defer here the way there is for remove/wishlist. So I read `checkoutOwner` via `useCountryConfig()` and navigate via `useNavigation()` **inside** the component, both called directly (no props). `useNavigation()` used directly inside a `ui-kits/` leaf is already precedented — `zimmSearchInput/index.tsx` does exactly this today. Full reasoning is in the component's own "Architecture note" docblock and decision-log item 5. If a future step needs to override the destination, that's a small additive prop later, not a reason to build one now for a caller that doesn't exist yet. One consequence: "domestic, both auth states" and "international, both auth states" are behaviourally **identical** in this component (it takes no auth prop) — I wrote them as two separate, clearly-labelled tests anyway (matching how your Tester brief names them as two cases) rather than collapsing them, so the AC mapping stays explicit even though the assertions are the same. --- ### Other disclosed decisions (flagged in code + here, not buried) 1. **`checkoutOwner: 'hybrid'` (US) treated as domestic**, grouped with `'sfcc'` — only `'global-e'` hides the express buttons. `CheckoutOwner`'s own doc comment groups US with AU/GB/EU as "SFCC owns domestic paths," and every international example named anywhere in the plan/session-notes (HK, ME) is `'global-e'` — none is `'hybrid'`. Plan.md's own AC text only describes two cases ("domestic"/"international"), not the type's real three values. This is a plausible, evidenced reading, not a certain one — worth your eyes. 2. **Apple Pay / Google Pay show visible text next to the logo** ("APPLE PAY" / "GOOGLE PAY", uppercase caption text — see the live screenshot below), not icon-only as Figma shows. `ZimmButton`'s labelled render path always renders `label` as visible text with no way to suppress it while keeping the string for `aria-label` — fixing that means extending the shared atom, out of this step's manifest. Confirmed live, not assumed. 3. **`useExpressCheckoutEnabled()` checked, not wired in** — per the plan's own instruction to check it first. It gates a different axis (device/browser eligibility, SFCC-309, not yet scoped) from the region-based hide this component owns; wiring it in would be scope nobody asked for this step. --- ### Pass criteria — what's proven and how 1. **Domestic: 3 children, fixed order** — Vitest (`getAllByRole` order check) + live Playwright against the real running Storybook: 3 buttons, `["Checkout","Apple Pay","Google Pay"]`. 2. **International: exactly 1 child, `queryByRole` null, height unchanged** — Vitest asserts `queryByRole('button', {name: /apple pay/i})` is `null` (not a visibility check). Height: live-measured via Playwright, not jsdom (jsdom can't do real layout) — Default root height **188px**, International root height **52px**. Arithmetic: 188 − 2×(52px button + 16px gap) = 188 − 136 = **52** — exact match, proving no compensating gap, live not assumed. 3/4. **Five states on Checkout (primary) and Pay buttons (secondary)** — default/hover/active/disabled existence-and-differs-from-default and focus-visible≠default all proven by reading `ZimmButton`'s own recipe object directly (same technique already established in `zimmQuantityStepper`'s test), because these states are 100% inherited from that already-shipped, already-tested atom — re-simulating real CSS `:hover`/`:focus-visible` in jsdom would be re-testing infrastructure this step correctly reuses, not builds (disclosed rather than left implicit — this is the one place I leaned on structural proof + the live screenshot's default-state colours rather than a live hover/focus simulation, consistent with this being a Light-scale step). One bug caught and fixed here: I initially assumed `primary._focusVisible` existed directly — it doesn't (`zimmButton.css.ts`'s own comment: "Focus ring inherited from baseStyle" for `primary` specifically) — test failed, fixed to read `Button.baseStyle._focusVisible` instead, now correct. 5. **Error-in-cart: all three enabled, zero feedback copy** — Vitest: no button `disabled`/`aria-disabled`, and `container.textContent` equals exactly the three button names concatenated, nothing else. Story exists and renders (see Storybook verification below). 6. **Navigation branches** — 4 Vitest tests (domestic×2 auth labels → `navigate('/checkout')`; international×2 auth labels → same, via the named, separately-unit-tested `navigateInternationalCheckoutStub`) plus a direct unit test of the stub function itself. 7. **`countries.ts` unmodified** — confirmed via `git status --porcelain`. 8. **Story title `'Commerce/ZimmCartButtonGroup'`** — confirmed in the file and live: Storybook's real index.json shows `commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--default/--international/--error-in-cart`. 9. **Blocked sub-item resolved** — marks exist and are used (as verified-identical inlined vector data — see the `` finding above for the one mechanism change from what was planned). **Mutation-tested** (Verification Standard #7): the "no compensating gap" recipe test (added a fake `height: '200px'` and a wrong gap var — both caught, then reverted) and the international-branch condition (mutated `checkoutOwner === 'global-e'` to a nonsense string — the "exactly one button" test correctly failed with "3 buttons" — then reverted via the `sed`-generated `.bak`, confirmed no stray file left behind). Did not mutation-test every one of the 22 assertions individually; the ones reading `ZimmButton`'s pre-existing recipe object are proving inheritance of already-tested infrastructure, not new logic. --- ### Storybook verification (Verification Standard #9 — actually done, not assumed) Ambient instance on `localhost:6006` was live and had already picked up the 3 new stories via its file-watcher (confirmed via `index.json` before touching anything). Ran `npx test-storybook --url http://localhost:6006 zimmcartbuttongroup` — **3/3 smoke tests PASS**, real headless Chromium, no error boundary. Then drove the actual rendered iframes directly with Playwright (correct IDs are `commerce-zimmcartbuttongroup--*` — the `Commerce/` category prefix is part of the real ID, a false start I caught by reading the real `index.json` rather than guessing) to get the live DOM counts/heights above and two screenshots. Visually: Checkout renders black/white/uppercase as expected; Apple/Google Pay render bordered, monochrome, correctly ordered — and visibly show the disclosed text-next-to-logo deviation from item 2 above. --- ### Gate output - `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, exit 0, no output. - `npm run test` — **123 test files passed, 1697 tests passed**, 0 failures (includes `recipeGuards.test.ts` 6/6, `recipeParts.test.ts` — actual path is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`, not under `theme/components/` as plan.md's prose might suggest — 49/49, and `theme/index.test.tsx` 128/128, all green with the new recipe registered). - `npx eslint` on all 5 touched files — **0 errors**. Fixed 2 real errors along the way (missing display-name + prettier formatting) by rewriting the stories file to use inline per-story decorators instead of a factory function, matching `zimmCartItemActions`' established story pattern exactly. Remaining 9 warnings are `@typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion` on `Button.variants!`/`Button.sizes!` reads — confirmed this exact warning already exists un-fixed on the precedent files (`zimmButton.css.test.ts`: 2, `zimmQuantityStepper/index.test.tsx`: 3) I copied the technique from, each with the same kind of justifying comment mine has. - `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — my 4 new named constants (Pay-mark/slot dimensions) are correctly recognised as **acknowledged exceptions** (the `audit-allow:` comment worked as intended). **Zero new unacknowledged violations.** The 9 unacknowledged violations the script reports are all in files outside my manifest that I never touched (`footer.css.ts`, `item-image.tsx`, `item-price.tsx`, `zimmIconAndText.css.ts`, `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts`, `zimmBenefits.css.ts`, `zimmDrawerShared.ts`) — pre-existing, not this step's to fix. --- ### Unverified gaps (my own blind spots, not proven either way) - Real browser `:hover`/`:focus-visible`/`:active` were not simulated live (mouse hover / keyboard Tab) in this pass — proven structurally (recipe object) and via the default-state screenshot only, per the Light-scale reasoning in pass criteria 3/4 above. - I did not verify this component against a real `ZimmCartDrawer` `footer` slot (step 4.6 doesn't exist yet) — only in isolation, per this step's own scope. --- ### What Marcel is missing The ``-doesn't-work-for-any-project-SVG constraint is currently documented in exactly two places: `ZimmLogo`'s component docblock, and now this component's decision log. It isn't in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, `conventions.md`, or anywhere a future step planner or implementer would think to check before reaching for `` on a new asset — which is exactly how it nearly shipped broken here too. Worth a one-line addition to the shared styling/conventions rules (not something I've touched, since it's outside this step's manifest) before a third occurrence has to re-discover it from scratch.

**The fix:** extend `ZimmButton` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx`) with a new prop on `ZimmLabelButtonProps` — something like `hideLabelVisually?: boolean` — that, when true, renders the label's `<chakra.span __css={labelStyle}>{label}</chakra.span>` (line 198) using Chakra's `VisuallyHidden` instead, so the label text still exists as an accessible text node but isn't visually rendered. `aria-label={label}` on the `ChakraButton` itself (line 184) is already always set regardless, so the accessible name doesn't depend on this change either way — this prop only affects the *visible* span. `VisuallyHidden` already has precedent in this codebase (`zimmDropdownItem`, `zimmProductCard`, `zimmGalleryOverlay`, `zimmProductGallery` all use it) — match whatever pattern those use rather than inventing a new one.

Apply `hideLabelVisually` to both the Apple Pay and Google Pay `<ZimmButton>` calls in `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx` (not the Checkout button — that one's label is genuinely visible per Figma, "CHECKOUT" renders as real button text). One smaller thing, not urgent, your call whether to touch it in the same pass: decision-log item 2's citation slightly overstates itself — it says `countries.ts`'s `CheckoutOwner` doc comment "groups US with AU/GB/EU as 'SFCC owns domestic paths'" in those words; I checked the actual comment and it doesn't say that literally (it just says "Checkout owner for this site's domestic path. Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field..."). Your underlying reasoning is still sound (`globalEPricing: false` for `hybrid`/US is a real, correct signal), just cite it as your own inference from the country data rather than as a direct quote from the doc comment. Small precision fix, not a logic change — fine to fold in with the main fix above.

After the fix: re-run the full gate set, re-verify live in Storybook that both Pay buttons now show icon-only (screenshot or Playwright DOM check, not just the source), and report back with what changed.

Address this before completing your current task.

input.message:
## Fix applied and independently re-verified live. Both Pay buttons are now icon-only, confirmed by screenshot + real bounding-box measurement, not just by reading the source.

### What changed, on top of the original step-5.1 report

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx`** (outside the original manifest — touched only after independently confirming via `CODEOWNERS` line 176 that `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` routes to the identical `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b` Tier 3 ownership as every file already in this step's manifest, so this isn't a multi-tier change, and after independently re-finding the `ariaDescribedBy`-on-icon-variant precedent myself in the file's own existing text, matching your citation):
- Added `hideLabelVisually?: boolean` to `ZimmLabelButtonProps`, documented as primary/secondary-only (social has its own separate label span untouched by this).
- The label render (was line 198, unconditional `<chakra.span __css={labelStyle}>{label}</chakra.span>`) now branches: `true` → `<VisuallyHidden>{label}</VisuallyHidden>`, else unchanged. `aria-label={label}` on the outer `ChakraButton` (line 184/195) was already unconditional, so the accessible name never depended on this — only the visible span changes.
- 4 new tests in `zimmButton`'s own suite (default-unchanged, explicit-false-unchanged, hidden-when-true via `getComputedStyle` on the real Chakra `visuallyHiddenStyle` values, icon-unaffected). Mutation-tested: reverted the render branch to always-visible, confirmed the "hidden when true" test fails with the exact expected diff (`'static'` vs `'absolute'`), restored, re-ran clean.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`**:
- `hideLabelVisually` added to both the Apple Pay and Google Pay `<ZimmButton>` calls, not Checkout.
- Decision-log item 3 rewritten to describe what's actually shipped (icon-only, fixed via the `ZimmButton` extension, coordinator-confirmed against a live Figma screenshot of node `9323:95939`) instead of the old disclosed-gap framing.
- Decision-log item 2's citation corrected per your note: no longer claims `CheckoutOwner`'s doc comment literally groups `'hybrid'` with `'sfcc'` — now states plainly that this is my own inference from the country data (`globalEPricing: false` for `hybrid`, matching `sfcc`, vs. `true` for every real `global-e` site), not a quote.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartButtonGroup/index.test.tsx`**: 3 new tests — DOM-presence-but-not-visually-rendered (same `getComputedStyle` technique as the zimmButton test), accessible-name-still-resolves via `getByRole`, and a control assertion that Checkout's own label stays genuinely visible (not hidden — it's real Figma button text, not a mark). Mutation-tested by removing `hideLabelVisually` from the Apple Pay call only — the "not visually rendered" test correctly failed (`'static'` vs `'absolute'`) while everything else stayed green; restored, re-ran clean.

### Live re-verification — and one real tooling nuance worth flagging

Re-ran `test-storybook` — 3/3 stories still pass, no error boundary. Then drove the real rendered iframe with Playwright again:

- **Screenshot**: only the logo marks render now — the separate "APPLE PAY"/"GOOGLE PAY" caption text from the first screenshot is gone. Visually clean, icon-only, matches what you described from the Figma pull.
- **Direct measurement** of the label span: `boundingBox` = `{width: 1, height: 1}`, computed style = `position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0px, 0px, 0px, 0px)` — the exact, correctly-applied `@chakra-ui/visually-hidden` output.
- **One thing that could have misled me if I'd stopped at the first check**: Playwright's own `.innerText()` and `.isVisible()` both still report the label as "visible" text (`"APPLE PAY"` uppercase) for this element. That's not a bug in the fix — the 1×1px clip technique is deliberately designed to be invisible to human eyes while staying "in the render tree," and Playwright's visibility heuristics (non-zero bounding box + `display`/`visibility` checks) don't specifically special-case that pattern the way a screen reader's accessibility-tree walk does. The coordinator sent a message while you were working:
Tester found no blocking defects, but three small, cheap, real fixes worth making before this goes to Orchestrator/Scorer. All independently confirmed by the Tester with live evidence, not just source reads:

1. **Wrong semantic token on both Pay-mark fills.** `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx:70,95` use `useToken('colors', ['text.default'])` to colour an icon/logo glyph — but `theme/foundation/colour.ts` already registers a separate `icon: {default: grey[900], disabled: grey[200]}` alias for exactly this case (`--zimm-color-icon-default` is already a live CSS var). Same numeric value today so nothing looks wrong on screen, but a future independent re-theme of text vs. icon colour would silently miscolour one of them. Change both to `useToken('colors', ['icon.default'])`. (Note: `zimmLogo/index.tsx` has the identical pre-existing issue — leave that alone, out of scope, already flagged separately.)

2. **Missing `preserveAspectRatio="none"` on both inlined `<chakra.svg>` elements.** Both source SVGs (`overrides/app/assets/svg/{apple,google}-pay-logo.svg`) carry this at the root; neither of your inlined copies does. Functionally inert today (both marks are live-measured rendering at their correct sizes since each has its own self-consistent `viewBox`/`width`/`height`), but it's a real source-fidelity gap — if the slot-sizing logic ever changes, this missing attribute could silently reintroduce distortion risk with nothing to catch it. Add `preserveAspectRatio="none"` to both `<chakra.svg>` elements to match the source exactly.

3. **`hideLabelVisually` has zero Storybook coverage.** Only Vitest exercises the new `ZimmButton` prop — `components.md` expects a story for a meaningful new visual state, and this one changes a labelled button into a visually icon-only one, which is exactly the kind of thing a story exists to show. Add a story to `zimmButton/index.stories.tsx` demonstrating `hideLabelVisually: true` (e.g. reuse the Apple Pay button shape, or any icon+label combination) so it's visible in isolation, not just provable via computed-style assertions in a test file.

Two more things the Tester found, real but explicitly **not for you to fix** — already logged in `handoff.md` as decisions only Marcel can make, not engineering gaps: (a) `checkoutOwner: 'hybrid'` can't currently be branched by real shipping destination because that signal doesn't exist anywhere in the codebase yet — your interim always-domestic treatment is the only currently-answerable reading, correctly built; (b) the base `/cart` page has no redirect into the new drawer, which is a scope question for a later commit, not this step's. Don't touch either.

After the three fixes: re-run the full gate set once more, confirm the new `ZimmButton` story renders live in Storybook, and report back.

Address this before completing your current task.

## All three Tester-found fixes applied and independently re-verified live. Full gate set green.

### 1. Fixed: wrong semantic colour alias on both Pay-mark fills

Independently re-confirmed the claim first (`theme/foundation/colour.ts:91-94` — `icon: {default: grey[900], disabled: grey[200]}`, and `zimmTokens.ts:83` — `'--zimm-color-icon-default': colors.icon.default` — both real, already-live). Changed `useToken('colors', ['text.default'])` → `useToken('colors', ['icon.default'])` in both `ApplePayMark` and `GooglePayMark` (`zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`), each with an inline comment explaining why the semantically-correct alias matters even though it's numerically identical today. Live-confirmed via Playwright reading the actual rendered `<path fill="...">` in the browser: both resolve to `#191919`, matching `icon.default`'s real value — no visual change, correct alias now.

### 2. Fixed: missing `preserveAspectRatio="none"` on both inlined SVGs
